messages.subject: data analysis
parts:
Hi,
I am trying to do some data anlysis. I have a csv file (attached) which contains some feature vectors.
The vectors are grouped into various groups (Counter,F1-F4, G1-G2, H1-H2).
I need to do some cleanup on these values (some of them are invalid). For each group, I have a different cleanup function which uses the value and one or more appropriate values from other columns.
An example of such a cleanup function would be to extract the number from F# and then compare that number to the counter (so F2 should be calculated as NA if Counter is 2 or smaller).

I tried to do something like this:
# read the features from a file
feature_list=read.csv(file='C:\\git\\example.csv');

# get the names vector
feature_names = names(feature_list);

create_names <- function (single_feature_name) {
  clean_function1 <- function (something) {
    something[something>500] = NA;
    return(something);
  }
  clean_function2 <- function (something) {
    something[something<1000] = NA;
    return(something);
  }
  clean_function3 <- function (something) {
    something[something>800] = NA;
    return(something);
  }
  if(single_feature_name %in% paste("F", 1:4, sep="")) {
    the_func=clean_function1;
  } else {
    if(single_feature_name %in% paste("G", 1:2, sep="")) {
      the_func=clean_function2;
    } else {
      the_func=clean_function3;
    }   
  }
  result = list(feature_name=single_feature_name, num_levels=10, clean_func=the_func);
  return(result);
}

#get data on each function
features_structure = lapply(feature_names,create_names);

#cleanup
cleaned_features=lapply(feature_list,missing_func);


My problem is this:
1. How should the clean_function be defined so I can test the values from other columns (i.e. instead of working doing the condition something>500 I want do some something like other_column>500)
2. How should I call this function? lapply assumes the function is specific while I need to call the specific clean_func inside features_structures (which should be of the same column).
3. is there a better way to decide on the function (I wanted to do a switch but couldn't figure out how to do expression in the switch and didn't want to do a switch for each single feature)

Thanks.

messages.author: a305e65fa9dfb74d
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] data analysis
parts:
This code has a strong OO flavor to it. :-)


1. For this type of cleaning, lapply() will surely not work as you are not operating column-wise. 

2. I think the problem is that you want the first lapply to return a list within a list, and it returns a flat list.
Here is some code that might do what you want, but as you can see, it is not a very natural way:

features_structure = Map(feature_names,f=create_names);
functions<- lapply(features_structure, function(x) x$clean_func)
listted.fature_list<- lapply(feature_list, list)
mapply(do.call, functions, listted.fature_list)


3. Is it important to solve it with a single function and not with a script?

parts:
Thanks for the quick reply.
First I'd like to make sure I understood what you did:

> features_structure = Map(feature_names,f=create_names);
If I understand correctly this create a list which has a name for each feature so this would be a far better way of doing
features_structure = lapply(feature_names,create_names);
names(features_structure)<-feature_names;
right?
>functions<- lapply(features_structure, function(x) x$clean_func)

This basically creates a vector where for each feature we have a function (so I can even create a singular function for each feature if I wanted to.
>listted.fature_list<- lapply(feature_list, list)
this just turns the feature_list data frame into a list so we can work with each feature (column) as a single list element with the correct name.
> mapply(do.call, functions, listted.fature_list)
so if I understand correctly this calls do.call(arg1,arg2) where arg1 and arg2 are the same index of the two lists: functions and listted.fature_list which basically means we do do.call(feature_function, feature_values) which in turn calls feature_function with feature_values as a parameter?

Now if I understood this correctly, I still have a couple of elements missing:
1. how do I get info on another column? I guess I can provide additional arguments to do.call (e.g. by using MoreArgs=lissted.fature_list and then directly accessing the relevant column but is there a more elegant solution for that?
2. The deciding of the function part. I am already writing everything in a script, the problem is I have close to 1000 features (the example here is condensed considerably). I don't want to have 1000 lines. The features are divided into ~50 groups so I prefer to write in the function a line for each of the 50 instead of one for each of the 1000 :). In any case it would look something like XXX_i_YYY_j where i and j are numbers which run in a range (so for example I might have 100 features which are FEATURE_i_SUBFEATURE_j where i and j are numbers between 0 to 9). I can do that with lots of if/else clauses but I would much prefer something more condensed. Switch would be good if I could add an expression in there but it seems I can't so I am looking for something a little more elegant.

Thanks
